t:
(a) 
During fiscal year 1979, the Secretary of Defense, in carrying out the Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding Between the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) Ministers of Defence on the NATO E–3A Cooperative Programme, signed by the Secretary of Defense on December 6, 1978, may—

        (1) 
waive reimbursement for the cost of the following functions performed by personnel other than personnel employed in the United States Air Force Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) program office:

            (A) 
auditing;
 
            (B) 
quality assurance;
 
            (C) 
codification;
 
            (D) 
inspection;
 
            (E) 
contract administration;
 
            (F) 
acceptance testing;
 
            (G) 
certification services; and
 
            (H) 
planning, programming, and management services;
  
        (2) 
waive any surcharge for administrative services otherwise chargeable; and
 
        (3) 
in connection with the NATO E–3A Cooperative Programme for fiscal year 1979, assume contingent liability for—

            (A) 
program losses resulting from the gross negligence of any contracting officer of the United States;
 
            (B) 
identifiable taxes, customs duties, and other charges levied within the United States on the program; and
 
            (C) 
the United States share of the unfunded termination liability.
   
    (b) 
Authority under this section to enter into contracts shall be effective for any fiscal year only to such extent or in such amounts as are provided in appropriation Acts.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the Memorandum of Understanding with NATO defence ministers shows coordination with parties outside the federal government. But that agreement was already signed in the past, and the section only authorizes the Secretary of Defense to waive certain charges and assume contingent liabilities in carrying it out. Nothing here requires or invites consultation, comment, hearings, an advisory body, or a right to sue involving any outside party before a federal decision.
fable.s: in carrying out the Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding Between the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) Ministers of Defence on the NATO E–3A Cooperative Programme, signed by the Secretary of Defense on December 6, 1978

opus.w: This section gives the Secretary of Defense financial powers: waiving reimbursements and surcharges and assuming contingent liability under an existing NATO agreement. It does not require any comment period, hearing, advisory body or consultation with outside parties before those decisions. The reference to an agreement with NATO defence ministers looks like participation, but it describes an agreement signed in the past. As in the earlier example about the 1946 mine safety agreement, a past agreement is not future participation in a federal decision.
opus.s: in carrying out the Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding Between the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) Ministers of Defence on the NATO E–3A Cooperative Programme, signed by the Secretary of Defense on December 6, 1978, may—
opus.b: The section might look like participation at first because it refers to a "Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding" with NATO defence ministers, who are outside the federal government. That reading doesn't hold up. The memorandum was already signed (December 6, 1978). The section only lets the Secretary of Defense waive reimbursement and surcharges and take on contingent liability. Nothing requires consulting outsiders before those decisions.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of Defense to waive costs and assume liabilities related to a NATO program. While NATO involves foreign governments, the text does not require the Secretary to consult with or coordinate with those foreign entities or any other outside parties before making these decisions. The actions described are internal administrative and financial decisions made by federal officials. Therefore, there is no participation by outside parties in the decision-making process described in this section.
qwen_chat.s: During fiscal year 1979, the Secretary of Defense, in carrying out the Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding Between the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) Ministers of Defence on the NATO E–3A Cooperative Programme, signed by the Secretary of Defense on December 6, 1978, may— (1) waive reimbursement for the cost of the following functions performed by personnel other than personnel employed in the United States Air Force Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) program office... (3) in connection with the NATO E–3A Cooperative Programme for fiscal year 1979, assume contingent liability for— (A) program losses resulting from the gross negligence of any contracting officer of the United States...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "NATO E-3A Cooperative Programme" involves coordination with foreign governments (NATO members), which are outside the U.S. federal government. However, the text itself does not describe a process of consultation or participation with these entities; it merely authorizes the Secretary of Defense to waive certain costs and assume liabilities *within* the context of an existing agreement. The actors performing the actions in this section (Secretary of Defense, contracting officers, personnel) are all inside the federal government. There is no requirement for the Secretary to consult with NATO members, the public, or any other outside party before making the decisions authorized here.
